analysis.method: offline consistency check only (no network, no credential values output)

api_key_has_typical_prefix.meaning: the configured key does NOT start with sk-/volc-/eyJ (JWT). This is a format observation, NOT proof of invalidity — gateway-specific prefixes vary. But combined with the observed AuthenticationError it is the one config-side datum that does not self-confirm consistency.
api_key_has_typical_prefix.implication: possible causes remain open: credential mapping to this gateway, key scope/rotation, auth scheme expected by the gateway, or the key itself. The offline check cannot discriminate further.

analysis.conclusion: All structural/config consistency checks PASS (provider/model/endpoint/env plumbing all match expectations). The only non-confirming datum is the key prefix format, which is informational. The AuthenticationError therefore cannot be attributed to config plumbing on our side; it most likely lies in the credential-gateway relationship (validity/scope/scheme), which only the user can verify.
